reason: Restraint on the tenant's IT business after it hands back possession (Exit Date, defined in cl. 15). No sale of goodwill, so Exception 1 cannot apply. The 3 km radius and the rent-free consideration do not save it.
Restricts only how the premises are used during the term. The tenant is free to run a co-working business anywhere else.
The right to the deposit and interest is extinguished, and the landlord discharged, if no claim is made in 90 days. Void under s.28(b).

The landlord's own computation of charges is final, and the clause expressly overrides the arbitration clause (cl. 22) and shuts out every forum. An absolute restriction for that class of dispute; void under s.28(a) to that extent.

Operates only during the Term (Section 3) but restrains business elsewhere in the Layout, not just use of the premises. In-term restraints are generally upheld (Golikari, Gujarat Bottling), but a landlord has a weak interest here. Refer.
A plain post-term non-compete. No goodwill sold. Void, however short the period or small the area.
A written agreement to refer a difference that has already arisen (the area of the demised room) to the GTC-42 panel. Saved by Exception 2.

Chooses the courts of the district where the property is situated (Madhapur is in Ranga Reddy District) and the High Court. Those courts have jurisdiction anyway. Valid (Hakam Singh, A.B.C. Laminart).
A notice step so the landlord can claim on its insurance. Nothing is lost if the notice is late.
The landlord limits how it lets the rest of its own building, only during the lease. A restriction on dealing with property, not on the landlord's trade.

Arbitration happens only if both agree at the time, so there is no binding arbitration agreement (Jagdish Chander). Yet the courts are barred 'in any event', and cl. 18 no longer names a court. If either side refuses to arbitrate there is no forum at all. Exception 1 does not save it.
A snag-list step. No right is lost if the tenant reports late.

The tenant is 'released and discharged' if the landlord does not notify damage within 45 days. This discharges liability on expiry of a period, so it is void under s.28(b). The section protects the landlord as much as the tenant.

The seller of the cafeteria goodwill restrains itself, within specified local limits, for as long as the buyer carries on the business. All the conditions of Exception 1 are met, so validity turns on whether the limits are reasonable, which is for the court. Refer.

Names the courts at New Delhi for a Bangalore property, and the arbitration is held at Bangalore. Delhi may have jurisdiction over some money claims (one lessor resides there), but not over the property itself. The text alone does not settle it. Refer.
Limits the time to sue or arbitrate to 6 months, against the 3 years the Limitation Act allows. Void under s.28(a).
A liquidated damages clause. Whether 6 months' rent on top of lock-in rent is a penalty is a s.74 question, outside ss.27–28. Refer.

Bars every suit, arbitration or proceeding over utility failures, which are the landlord's obligations under cl. 14(o). An absolute restriction for that class of claims; void under s.28(a) to that extent.

A binding arbitration agreement under the 1996 Act, saved by Exception 1. Unilateral appointment of the sole arbitrator by the Lessors is bad under Perkins Eastman and CORE, but that goes to appointment, not to s.28.
The Lessors are discharged if no claim is notified within the Claim Period, which cl. 26 defines as 60 days. Void under s.28(b).
